title: Bonds Hold Ground Despite Some Healing in Tech
summary:
Bonds Hold Ground Despite Some Healing in Tech 

             
             
            Monday was exceptionally uneventful for the bond market--as is more often than not the case for data-free Mondays without any other major developments. There were some minor developments though. Tech stocks bounced back a bit, closing at their best level since last Wednesday. Corporate bond yields for Coreweave (a recent focal point for tech sector contagion potential) also moved slightly lower. On most recent occasions, that would imply upward pressure on mortgage rates. In that light, today's sideways performance was a victory.

title: Mortgage Rates Hold Steady Over The Weekend
summary: It was an uneventful day for mortgage rates, which is just the sort of thing you want to see when the average lender is just a hair above the lowest levels in more than a month. There were no significant economic reports or other market developments that caused any major volatility for rates/bonds.  The dominant theme, of late, has been investor rotation out of AI-related assets and into the bond market. Excess demand for bonds is good for rates, all else equal. But there's a nuance. Corporate bonds related to certain tech companies have seen sharply lower demand. That's actually been good for mortgage rates and Treasuries because the tech-related corporate bonds had been drawing demand away from the safer mortgage/Treasury debt.   Today's ground-holding is all the more encouraging considering there was some healing in the tech sector, both in terms of stock prices and corporate bond demand.  Simply put, mortgage rates held steady despite slight headwinds elsewhere in the market.

title: Secure Insight Names Rob Chrisman To Board Of Directors
summary: Secure Insight has appointed mortgage industry veteran Rob Chrisman to its board of directors, adding one of the industry's most recognizable commentators and capital markets professionals to its leadership ranks as the company expands its mortgage fraud prevention and risk management business.Chrisman, whose career spans more than 40 years in mortgage banking, capital markets, and executive advisory services, will help guide the New Jersey-based fintech company's strategic direction, market positioning, business development, and long-term growth initiatives.

title: Luxury Home Price Growth Outpaces Starter Homes In Roughly 70% Of Major Markets
summary: Higher-end homes are posting stronger price growth than starter homes across much of the country, revealing a split in the purchase market that the national slowdown alone does not capture.Luxury-tier home price appreciation outpaced starter-tier appreciation in roughly 70% of the major markets First American Data & Analytics tracks, according to its September Home Price Index report. Chief Economist Mark Fleming attributed the difference to buyers’ uneven ability to absorb higher financing costs.

title: FICO Ties $10 Mortgage Score Pricing To Lender Commitments
summary: FICO is offering lenders and brokers a hold on its $10 wholesale mortgage score price in exchange for a commitment to keep buying its scores.The company announced last week that lenders and brokers enrolled in its Preferred Program through participating tri-merge resellers will receive Classic FICO and FICO Score 10T as a bundle at the same wholesale price as a year earlier. Eligibility is tied to lenders having committed to FICO through those partners.

title: Beeline Announces Job Cuts While Pursuing Non-QM Growth
summary: Beeline Holdings is pairing its push into Non-QM lending with planned workforce reductions, pursuing a smaller expense base even after forecasting its strongest quarterly revenue in five years.The combination brings the economics behind its product shift into focus: management credits bank statement and debt-service-coverage-ratio loans with improving performance, while continuing to pursue positive operating cash flow.

title: Northpointe Plans Retail Mortgage Exit, Pursues CMG Deal
summary: Northpointe Bank plans to exit distributed retail and consumer direct mortgage origination and transition those teams to CMG Financial, with management saying production could no longer support the overhead required to operate the business.The proposed move would give CMG another opportunity to expand through an established origination team while Northpointe directs more resources toward financing other mortgage lenders.

title: UWM Plans Up To $80B MSR Sale To Pay Down Debt
summary: United Wholesale Mortgage plans to sell servicing rights tied to $70 to $80 billion in mortgages during the fourth quarter, turning a substantial portion of its servicing portfolio into cash for debt repayment.UWM Holdings disclosed the planned sales Friday, Oct. 23, alongside preliminary third-quarter results. It expects proceeds exceeding $1.8 billion and said that money, together with $400 million in anticipated gross proceeds from its rights offering, would support the ongoing paydown of non-funding debt.
